knowledge:
- key_parameters: conditions=unique conditions vector used to define comparisons ;; reference=index of the reference condition in the conditions vector ;; compNames=character vector of comparison names to visualize ;; sel_prots=indices or names of selected features/proteins to highlight in plots ;; testNames=character vector specifying which statistical tests to plot ;; qlim=FDR threshold for filtering significant features in UpSet plots ;; heatmap_scale=character indicating if the values should be centered and scaled in the row or column direction
- alternatives: VSClust (or its Shiny web application) for clustering features based on expression patterns ;; ComplexBrowser and CoExpresso web applications for investigating protein complexes
- when_to_use: When analyzing quantitative omics data (e.g., proteomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics) with low replicate numbers and many missing values (represented as NA) ;; When wanting to compare multiple statistical tests and combine them using a unified PolySTest FDR
- pitfalls: High missingness: Features with only minimal non-missing values should be removed before analysis ;; P-values out of range: Miss_test qvalue calculation can fail and fall back to Benjamini-Hochberg if p-values are not in the valid range [0, 1] ;; FDR correction fallback: If there are less than 200 p-values, the package falls back to the Benjamini-Hochberg method for FDR correction in t-test and permutation test ;; Overloaded plots: For plotExpression, users should reduce the number of features to a maximum of 20 to avoid overloaded plots

workflows.name: quantitative_omics_differential_testing
workflows.intent: Perform differential abundance testing on quantitative omics data with missing values using multiple statistical tests and visualize the results.
input: LiverAllProteins.csv (matrix of quantitative features as rows and samples as columns, with missing values as NA)
sampleMetadata (data frame describing sample conditions and replicates)
workflows.stages: 1. Load and preprocess quantitative data (subsetting and median normalization) ;; 2. Construct a SummarizedExperiment object with assays, colData, rowData, and metadata ;; 3. Update conditions using update_conditions_with_lcs ;; 4. Define pairwise comparisons using create_pairwise_comparisons ;; 5. Run statistical testing using PolySTest_unpaired (or PolySTest_paired for matched samples) ;; 6. Visualize results using p-value distribution, volcano, UpSet, expression, regulation number, and heatmap plots
workflows.code:
library(PolySTest)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
# Load the data file "LiverAllProteins.csv" from the PolySTest package
filename <- system.file("extdata", "LiverAllProteins.csv", 
                        package = "PolySTest")

dat <- read.csv(filename, row.names=1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dat <- dat[1:200,] # Use a subset of the data for this example

# Normalization (example)
dat <- t(t(dat) - colMedians(as.matrix(dat), na.rm = TRUE))

sampleMetadata <- data.frame(Condition = rep(paste("Condition", 1:4), each=3),
                             Replicate = rep(1:3, each=4))

fulldata <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(quant = dat), 
                                 colData = sampleMetadata)
rowData(fulldata) <- rownames(dat)
metadata(fulldata) <- list(NumReps = 3, NumCond = 4)

assay(fulldata, "quant") <- dat

fulldata <- update_conditions_with_lcs(fulldata)

conditions <- unique(colData(fulldata)$Condition)

allComps <- create_pairwise_comparisons(conditions, 1)

fulldata_unpaired <- PolySTest_unpaired(fulldata, allComps)

# Define comparisons to visualize from available ones
compNames <- metadata(fulldata_unpaired)$compNames
print(compNames)
comps <- compNames[1]

# Plotting the results
plotPvalueDistr(fulldata_unpaired,  comps, c("limma", "Miss Test"))

# Select proteins with FDR < 0.01

sigProts <- which(rowData(fulldata_unpaired)[, paste0("FDR_PolySTest_", 
                                                      comps[1])] < 0.01)

# Volcano plot
plotVolcano(fulldata_unpaired, compNames = comps, sel_prots = sigProts, 
            testNames = c("PolySTest", "limma", "Miss Test"))

plotUpset(fulldata_unpaired, qlim=0.01)

plotExpression(fulldata_unpaired, sel_prots = sigProts)

plotRegNumber(fulldata_unpaired)

plotHeatmaply(fulldata_unpaired, sel_prots = sigProts, heatmap_scale = "row")
